title: Understanding Memory Allocation
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of understanding memory allocation and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply nbytes to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for understanding memory allocation.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 175 of the supplied curriculum: **Understanding Memory Allocation**. The main starting point is **nbytes**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Views and references can share memory, while copies own separate data. Awareness of this difference prevents accidental mutation and helps explain memory/performance trade-offs.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Understanding Memory Allocation** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **nbytes** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.float32)
print(a.nbytes)

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a slice owns independent memory
common_mistakes.why: Basic slicing commonly creates a view.
Short timings vary due to startup, cache, and system noise.
